payload.roles:
- THE WALKING AGENT - drives an iteration through the machine; the lane's heaviest user and the one whose behaviour changes if the lane is slower than the alternative.
- THE ARRIVING AGENT - a session with no memory of this project or of any law minted since its training; the role that exposes whether guidance actually reaches the packet, because it cannot know a rule it was not handed.
- THE OWNER-AS-ADJUDICATOR - rules the dependency choice and blesses gate_release; adjudicates the things a lint cannot.
- THE OWNER-AS-AUDITOR - reviews an iteration they did not watch, and must be able to tell a computed check from an asserted one. Distinct from the adjudicator role: adjudicating happens live, auditing happens after, and they need different things from the record.
- THE OWNER-AS-OPERATOR - installs, pairs, configures; the role that hits a missing config lane and a platform without an rg binary.
- THE RETRO - a role, not a person: the standing consumer of the call log, the se_help misses and the notes inbox. It is a stakeholder because tool-name double-counting and clauseless failures degrade ITS evidence specifically.
- THE FUTURE ITERATION - every iteration after this one inherits whatever this one builds; it is the stakeholder that pays for a weak lint forever.
- THE ENGINE ITSELF - self-hosting means the product under change is the tool doing the changing; it is a stakeholder in the sense that it must stay operable mid-iteration.
- THE EXTERNAL TOOL MAINTAINERS (ripgrep, git, @vscode/ripgrep) - not consulted, but depended upon; their stability is our assumption.
payload.tensions:
T1 WALKING AGENT vs ARRIVING AGENT - guidance volume. The walking agent already knows the rules and wants a short packet; the arriving agent knows nothing and needs every binding rule handed to it. The same join that serves one annoys the other. RULED: serve the arriving agent, because the walking agent skims cheaply and the arriving agent cannot recover what it never received - and relevance, not volume, keeps the cost down. This is se.raid-the-guidance-join-buries-the-instruction in stakeholder form.

T2 WALKING AGENT vs OWNER-AS-AUDITOR - speed against traceability. Every read routed through the lane is a logged read; the native tools are faster and silent. The agent's interest is throughput, the auditor's is knowing what was consulted. RULED: the lane must WIN on merit rather than by prohibition, because a prohibition the agent can route around produces exactly the silent reads the auditor loses. This is why 'path of least resistance' is the goal rather than 'lane is mandatory'.

T3 OWNER-AS-ADJUDICATOR vs OWNER-AS-AUDITOR - the same person, opposed interests, which is why the roles are split. The adjudicator wants to delegate everything and be absent; the auditor wants enough evidence to own the result afterwards. Delegation without computed checks serves the first and betrays the second. RULED by se.law-responsibility-never-delegates: the slider reaches zero, and what makes that safe is that the mechanical half is computed - so the auditor is served BY the thing that lets the adjudicator leave.

T4 OWNER-AS-OPERATOR vs THE NO-FALLBACK RULING - the operator on an unusual platform gets no search at all, where a fallback would have given them a slow one. The ruling favours the maintainer (no untested duplicate) over the operator (degraded service). NAMED, not resolved: the owner made this trade knowingly and it is recorded as an accepted assumption. The operator's mitigation is a documented manual install, not code.

T5 THE ENGINE ITSELF vs EVERY OTHER ROLE - self-hosting. Ripping out the searcher and rewriting dispatch changes the tools being used to do the ripping and rewriting, mid-flight. RULED, and it shapes the build order: land changes so the lane stays operable at every step, and expect that nothing built here reaches the LIVE surface until the merge - which is a limitation, not a defect, and is already recorded.

T6 THE RETRO vs EVERYONE - it wants the log to be clean, uniform and complete; nobody else feels the cost of a double-counted tool name or a clauseless failure. Its needs lose to scope here (log hygiene is a named non-goal), which is a deliberate under-service of a real stakeholder rather than an oversight.

NO TENSION FOUND between the future iteration and anyone: every role benefits from this landing well, which is itself a warning - a design where nobody objects usually means a stakeholder is missing from the map, and the one I am least confident I have represented is the operator on a platform I have never tested.
